data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for Canada summarizes key education-system characteristics using indicator results from OECD large-scale assessments and administrative/indicator sources. It highlights intergenerational educational inequality in tertiary attainment (e.g., a 36 percentage-point gap in tertiary attainment among 25–34 year-olds by parental education in 2023), trends in unemployment by educational attainment (including Canada’s higher unemployment levels than OECD averages for the least educated group), and labour-market differences by degree level (e.g., master’s holders’ higher employment and earnings). For adult skills, it reports literacy proficiency distributions from the Survey of Adult Skills/PIAAC (e.g., 20% at or below Level 1 in Canada) and literacy score changes between PIAAC Cycle 1 and Cycle 2. The note also covers access and progression in tertiary education (entry pathways, gender composition, completion and dropout patterns) and system investment indicators (expenditure per student and tuition fees for foreign students). Because it is a descriptive synthesis rather than an original student-level ML analysis, no predictive model performance metrics, PV handling, or missing-data strategy are provided in the note itself.
